html:
The Mojave, Pipa Aha Macav, "people by the river", are a Yuman-speaking people of the lower Colorado River, where Arizona, California and Nevada meet. The river's yearly floods let them grow maize, beans and pumpkins on the valley floor, in the middle of the Mojave Desert, which is named after them.

They were great travellers and fighters. Mojave runners crossed the desert along trails to trade with the coastal peoples of California. They were allies of the Quechan and enemies of the Maricopa. After clashes with emigrant parties, the US Army built Fort Mojave in their land in 1859. Today the Fort Mojave and Colorado River Indian Tribes reservations lie along the river. See also Chemehuevi.
